newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bourse, OM merger talks halted - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bourse, OM merger talks halted - newspaper.

text.p: Merger talks between the bourse and derivatives trader OM have halted after the finance ministry said it wanted the central securities depository to be included, Dagens Industri said on Friday.

"The information from the finance ministry has caused worries and right now nothing is happening with the negotiations," Bengt Ryden, head of the Stockholm stock exchange, was quoted by the newspaper as saying.
"We are waiting for clearer statements," he added.

Confusion arose after the finance ministry said in its April 15 spring budget proposal that it did not rule out including VPC (the central depository) in a group that would run other operations, including bourse operations.
The finance ministry also said it wanted parliament to allow it to sell its 50 percent stake in VPC and use the funds to help fund investments in the financial sector and infra-structure.
Analysts interpreted this to mean that the government wanted VPC to take part in the merger talks between OM and VPC.
But uncertainty prevailed, Ryden told the newspaper.
"Now we don't know in what order a merger can happen," Ryden was quoted as saying.
In an interview with Reuters in December 1996, Ryden said he expected a merger of all three players as an integrated market would bring more dynamism.
